signals.title: buf format v1.71+ regressions: non-idempotent inline block comments and stripped interior indentation
signals.text: ### Description `buf format` v1.71.0 introduced two regressions with the "Port new formatter" change: **Bug 1: Non-idempotent formatting of trailing line comments** Trailing `//` comments on option fields are converted to `/* */` block comments on the first pass (kept inline), then moved to a separate line on the second pass. The output never stabilizes in a single pass. **Repro (`example.proto`):** ```protobuf syntax = "proto3"; message Foo { bool bar = 1; // keep this inline } ``` **First `buf format` pass:** ```protobuf bool bar = 1; /* keep this inline */ ``` **Second `buf format` pass:** ```protobuf bool bar = 1; /* keep this inline */ ``` Running `buf format` twice produces different output — formatting is not idempotent. **Bug 2: Interior indentation alignment stripped from block comments** The formatter strips intentional interior indentation, destroying semantic alignment. Previously fixed in PR #1615 (v1.10.0) but reintroduced by the v1.71.0 new formatter port. **Repro:** ```protobuf syntax = "proto3"; service ExampleService { /** Reverse lookup a user from an identifier. - OK - response contains the resolved user id - NOT_FOUND - identifier was not found - INVALID_ARGUMENT - invalid identifier type - missing identifier - provided identifier is already USER_ID */ rpc GetUserId(GetUserIdRequest) returns (GetUserIdResponse); } message GetUserIdRequest {} message GetUserIdResponse {} ``` **`buf format` output (v1.72.0):** ```protobuf /** Reverse lookup a user from an identifier. - OK - response contains the resolved user id - NOT_FOUND - identifier was not found - INVALID_ARGUMENT - invalid identifier type - missing identifier - provided identifier is already USER_ID */ ``` The aligned sub-items under `INVALID_ARGUMENT` are flattened to the same indentation level as top-level list items, destroying the semantic grouping. "missing identifier" and "provided identifier is already USER_ID" are sub-cases of `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, not independent items. ### Expected behavior 1. Formatting should be idempotent — running `buf format` twice should produce the same output. 2. Interior indentation within block comments should be preserved (relative indentation maintained, as it was in v1.70.0 and earlier). ### Versions affected Both bugs affect v1.71.0+ (tested on v1.72.0). v1.70.0 does not have either issue.

signal.title: buf format v1.71+ regressions: non-idempotent inline block comments and stripped interior indentation
signal.text: ### Description `buf format` v1.71.0 introduced two regressions with the "Port new formatter" change: **Bug 1: Non-idempotent formatting of trailing line comments** Trailing `//` comments on option fields are converted to `/* */` block comments on the first pass (kept inline), then moved to a separate line on the second pass. The output never stabilizes in a single pass. **Repro (`example.proto`):** ```protobuf syntax = "proto3"; message Foo { bool bar = 1; // keep this inline } ``` **First `buf format` pass:** ```protobuf bool bar = 1; /* keep this inline */ ``` **Second `buf format` pass:** ```protobuf bool bar = 1; /* keep this inline */ ``` Running `buf format` twice produces different output — formatting is not idempotent. **Bug 2: Interior indentation alignment stripped from block comments** The formatter strips intentional interior indentation, destroying semantic alignment. Previously fixed in PR #1615 (v1.10.0) but reintroduced by the v1.71.0 new formatter port. **Repro:** ```protobuf syntax = "proto3"; service ExampleService { /** Reverse lookup a user from an identifier. - OK - response contains the resolved user id - NOT_FOUND - identifier was not found - INVALID_ARGUMENT - invalid identifier type - missing identifier - provided identifier is already USER_ID */ rpc GetUserId(GetUserIdRequest) returns (GetUserIdResponse); } message GetUserIdRequest {} message GetUserIdResponse {} ``` **`buf format` output (v1.72.0):** ```protobuf /** Reverse lookup a user from an identifier. - OK - response contains the resolved user id - NOT_FOUND - identifier was not found - INVALID_ARGUMENT - invalid identifier type - missing identifier - provided identifier is already USER_ID */ ``` The aligned sub-items under `INVALID_ARGUMENT` are flattened to the same indentation level as top-level list items, destroying the semantic grouping.
